page: Microsoft Azure E16nds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is configured with an Intel x86_64 architecture featuring 16 dedicated virtual CPUs. The system incorporates 128.0 GB of RAM, providing an allocation of 8.0 GB of memory per core. This dedicated processor assignment and expanded memory-to-core ratio ensure consistent compute execution and memory bandwidth without CPU oversubscription.

Storage and network characteristics reflect the specific design of the Endv6 series. The instance includes 944 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage, designed for temporary data, high-throughput caching, and low-latency scratch operations. In addition to the local NVMe drive, the instance supports Premium Storage integration for persistent volume configurations. The system is also designated as network-optimized, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the instance concentrates physical resources on high memory density and fast local disk capacity while omitting graphics processing units entirely. This makes the allocation cost-efficient for memory-centric operational workloads rather than parallel GPU tasks. The hardware profile is aligned with memory-bound workloads, including relational database engines, in-memory caches, big data analytics engines, and enterprise backend applications requiring local scratch space.
description: Microsoft Azure E16nds_v6 is a memory-optimized instance powered by an Intel x86_64 processor under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 16 dedicated vCPUs paired with 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Storage architecture includes a bundled 944 GB local NVMe solid-state drive alongside support for Premium Storage tiers. The instance belongs to the network-optimized Endv6 series and operates without integrated hardware accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With its balance of high memory density and high-speed local disk capacity, resource efficiency is concentrated on memory-bound and scratch-intensive scenarios rather than GPU-driven or compute-dense pipelines. The hardware configuration makes the instance suitable for in-memory databases, memory-resident data caching, intermediate analytics processing, and enterprise application deployments needing reliable memory headroom with fast temporary local I/O.
